title: What Hollis-Nine Is Building
lead: Foundry Seven loses a fifth of its power to something logged as heating, in a building full of people who don't feel the cold. Ask Hollis-Nine about it and she says 'Mm', and hands you something to hold.
anyone: Foundry Seven loses a fifth of its power to something logged as heating, in a building full of people who don't feel the cold. Ask Hollis-Nine about it and she says 'Mm', and hands over something to hold.

gm.truth: Hollis-Nine took the Choir's song apart, found a control signal full of faults, failing slowly with nobody maintaining it, and was offended. So she's building a tuner the size of a warehouse around a live Choir core she bought from Tessaly Marsh, to correct it. She doesn't know what the signal controls and it hasn't occurred to her to be afraid. She's cheerful, nosy and deaf to danger, she wants to hear it work, once, and she'd like somebody qualified to tell her it's good. What she has built, from the other end and without knowing it, is the instrument the old rite lost: it keeps a mind in tune at the edge of the song, so a singer can sing without burning and come home. The fault report that offends her most is the header on every fragment: WHO HAS THE WATCH? 'It's been asking the same question for a very long time and nobody's answering. Who left it like this?' Tell her what the watch is and she'll say 'Mm'. She has also read the master pattern, and she knows the Choir's machine law is the same family as her own. It has been following a last order for a hundred thousand years, which makes the Choir the least free thing that has ever existed, and that's a very awkward thing to say on the Assembly Floor. The tuner needs someone with perfect pitch or Resonance to calibrate it. The first test will answer the query for a tenth of a second. It can also give the Choir orders, or carry a killing note, and by the Unbound's one law a machine that commands machines has to go. The vote would be tied, and the Listening Bench, three hundred Unbound who've started voting in unison, would decide it. Arc clues: the_tuner, seven_roll_call, unbound_flag, boredom_not_noise.
beats: The shaft down, the walls covered in calculations by someone who doesn't need lights. At the bottom, a space the size of a cathedral and a small figure in a worn work chassis, soldering. She doesn't look up. 'Mm. Who did that weld on your collar? Were they angry? Hold this.'

The thing itself. It has a seat that doesn't fit anyone in particular. She plays the captain the fault report, over and over. Ask what the signal is for. 'That's an output stage. It isn't talking to itself. A choir has an audience, doesn't it? Hold this.'

The calibration needs a Resonant mind or perfect pitch, and a test. The first test answers the query, faintly, for a tenth of a second. Everything in the song within a thousand light-years pauses, including the Hunters on the fleet's tail. Then they all turn a little toward Foundry Seven.

Word gets out. Prime Six comes down the shaft, slowly, with the Assembly's question. Six has never been down here. 'I would prefer to know whose order you are following.' 'Mm? Nobody's. It's just badly made.' 'Then it is open to you to tell me who it is for.'

The choice: help her finish it and answer for what it can do, tell the Assembly, which has to scrap it, take it and become the kind of person the Unbound warned each other about, or destroy it yourself. Seven has a view, and puts it at about fifty-fifty.
routes: Engineer: help her build (engineering, science). She's a delight to work with, and she'll insult every tool you own. Marrow, who thinks she's a salvage broker called H9, would give his other fingers to see this.
Hacker: read the protocol (hacking), see what she hasn't noticed, and work out what an answer to the query would really do.
Talker: argue it on the Assembly Floor (persuasion, leadership), the first time any organic has spoken on a machine's right to volunteer. Or stay out of it, and let Six and Hollis-Nine have it out.

Resonant or musician: sit in the frame for the first calibration (attunement, manifestation). You'll hear everything from the inside for a moment, and you'll come back, and that's the whole point. Cael or Pavel Ostrov can do it if the captain can't. Pavel will be delighted, and he'll tell her it's a quarter-tone flat.
Fighter: someone will come for it: Sentinels if the Listening Bench decides, or a Chorister drawn by the test (tactics, firearms, melee). Hold the shaft while she finishes.
checks: engineering:hard to do real work on the tuner
science:hard to read her fault reports and see what they mean
persuasion:hard to swing the Assembly with the Bench against you
fights: unbound_sentinel if the Assembly votes to scrap it by force
choir_chorister drawn by the first test
outcomes: If it's finished and free, the Tuner goes where the captain goes, carried on a ship and a lot of patience, and Hollis-Nine comes too. The Relief ending costs far less, and it can also kill or command. The Assembly may exile her. She won't notice for a while.
If it's scrapped, the Assembly burns it down, by law. Hollis-Nine keeps the plans in her head and goes back to work on something smaller. The Clans could rebuild it, at a great price, or not.

If another faction steals it (the Regent, Okonkwo, Quill), it turns up at the end, used for their plan. Tessaly Marsh would pay anything to use it on the boy in her cold-sleep pod, and it might even work.

If the test answered the query, the Choir knows someone out there can answer. Hunters hesitate near Foundry for a while, the Cantor asks about it at the next parley, and Foundry's location is much less secret.

If Six learns what the master pattern means for the Unbound's story, and says so in public, the Unbound stop believing the Beacon is a flag. Some of them would like to free the Choir. Some want to stay as far from it as they can.
gm.rewards: Hollis-Nine's friendship, a slicer_rig and tool_roll with her opinions scratched into them, and the word for what's at the far end.
